note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Low-rank bottleneck of attention and high-rank structured scoring functions

nodes.name: Attention is a general tool with task-dependent biases
nodes.description: Softmax attention has inductive biases that suit some tasks better than others, and it is computationally expensive in runtime and memory.

nodes.name: Scoring function is a low-rank bilinear form
nodes.description: The attention scoring function takes a dot product of low-dimensional queries and keys, equivalent to a bilinear form with a rank-r matrix where the head dimension r is much smaller than the embedding dimension D.

nodes.name: Low-rank bottleneck
nodes.description: The low-rank scoring function loses token information for tasks with intrinsically high-dimensional inputs; for example it cannot represent s(x,x')=x^T x'.

nodes.name: Full-rank heads beat low-rank multi-head attention
nodes.description: Prior work shows one full-rank attention head can significantly outperform low-rank multi-head attention in in-context linear regression after controlling for model size.

nodes.name: BTT and MLR scoring functions are high rank and efficient
nodes.description: Block Tensor-Train (BTT) and contiguous Multi-Level Low Rank (MLR) matrices have high rank while remaining parameter- and compute-efficient, and replace the low-rank product in the attention scoring function (Bilinear BTT, Bilinear MLR).

nodes.name: Standard 8-head attention fails in-context regression
nodes.description: On in-context regression with input dimension 128, standard 8-head attention cannot learn the task even at model width D=512, while 1-head attention (r=D, full rank) learns it at D=512.

nodes.name: Bilinear BTT solves it at smaller width
nodes.description: Bilinear BTT with 8 heads is full rank and learns the in-context regression task at only D=256.

nodes.name: Bilinear BTT and MLR beat attention per compute
nodes.description: At fixed width D=256, both Bilinear MLR and Bilinear BTT attain lower regression error than 1-head or 8-head attention when controlling for training compute.

components.description: Distance-dependent compute bias with MLR attention

nodes.name: Standard attention has no distance-dependent compute bias
nodes.description: Standard attention scores every token pair with the same function and weights, and each token can attend to the whole context, which is expensive for long contexts.

nodes.name: Real data exhibits locality
nodes.description: Real-world datasets often exhibit locality, meaning a token's semantics depend most strongly on nearby tokens.

nodes.name: Contiguous MLR encodes distance-dependent compute
nodes.description: Using contiguous MLR for the attention score matrix gives nearby tokens higher-rank interactions and distant tokens cheaper ones, saving FLOPs compared to standard attention while keeping high-quality scores for neighbours.

nodes.name: MLR beats standard attention on OpenWebText
nodes.description: With 6-layer character-level transformers on OpenWebText (T=1024, r=64, D in {256,384,512,768}), 8-level MLR attention (rank split 32|8|6|4|4|4|4|2) outperforms standard attention at all widths throughout training, giving a better scaling law.

nodes.name: MLR beats sliding window variants
nodes.description: When controlling for compute, MLR attention outperforms sliding window attention (window 128) and a Global+SWA hybrid across model widths.

nodes.name: MLR cuts cost for Chronos time-series
nodes.description: Replacing T5 attention in Chronos with 6-level MLR attention (rank split 32|10|8|8|4|2) yields slightly lower validation loss with fewer FLOPs for embedding dimensions 128 to 512.

nodes.name: MLR improves long-horizon ETT forecasting
nodes.description: On the ETT dataset, MLR attention increasingly outperforms standard attention in oil temperature prediction as the forecast horizon grows.

isolated_nodes.name: Unifying MLBTC family
isolated_nodes.description: BTT and contiguous MLR (including Monarch, Butterfly, Kronecker and low-rank matrices as special cases) fall under a broader family called Multi-Level Block Tensor Contraction (MLBTC).

isolated_nodes.name: Language modeling does not show rank bottleneck
isolated_nodes.description: Some tasks including language modeling do not seem to suffer from the low-rank bottleneck.

isolated_nodes.name: muP transfer for MLR
isolated_nodes.description: Learning rates transfer stably across width for MLR attention when adapting Maximum Update Parameterization (muP).

structural_reasoning: Two uses of structured matrices in the attention score: high-rank BTT/MLR fixes the low-rank bottleneck, and MLR encodes locality to improve compute efficiency.
